title: GoPro’s IPO in June of 2014. It’s no secret that GoPro Inc
text:
GoPro’s IPO in June of 2014. 
It’s no secret that GoPro Inc (NASDAQ: GPRO ) has disappointed investors since its IPO in 2014. On that day, GoPro’s stock surged 30% in its trading debut and ended the day at $31.34 a share. Since then, GoPro has actually fallen far below its initial trading price. Leading up to its IPO, GoPro released a series of risk factors to its investors for the foreseeable future. These were the possibility that its ambitions would not reach fruition, the competitive nature of the hardware market, and the dependence the company puts on its CEO Nicholas Woodman. If you sit down and analyze GoPro today, it is clear to see that they did not properly manage these risk factors. Today, investors are paying for it.
The proof of that exists in GoPro’s share price of 6.02. Since July of 2015, the stock has fallen 93% from its high of 86.97. It seems like the market got caught up in the allure of GoPro’s product and did not recognize the failing financials. GoPro has struggled to expand beyond the extreme sports niche and industry rival Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) has been giving the high performance wearable camera producer a lot of trouble.
Product outlook for 2018 
Yet, some believe that 2018 is the year for GoPro. They have several new products that have the potential to bring GoPro back above their IPO price. One of these products is the GoPro Fusion. What makes this camera special is its ability to capture spherical video that is essential to virtual reality. VR undoubtedly has a stronger demand than action camera recording does and if the Fusion proves to be successful, GoPro could have a strong hold on that market. Investors are also waiting for the release of the Hero6 camera but will unfortunately not get the chance to see the Karma drone. This is a tough pill for investors to swallow because those who had stuck around had hoped that the drone would expand GoPro’s business further than just the camcorder market.
